subject: Request: interoperability & supply-chain attestation + CAIQ/SBOM evidence
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@nimblehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nimble Health Security <security@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Supply-chain and interoperability evidence request (SOC2/SIG/CAIQ)

Ben —

Thanks for the intro earlier this week. As part of our procurement and security onboarding for the upcoming integration project, our InfoSec team needs a compact evidence bundle focused on supply-chain and interoperability controls. Specifically we need: 

- Up-to-date subprocessor roster (including subprocessors used for embeddings, telemetry, logging and KMS) with service descriptions and data flow boundaries.
- The top-layer SBOM or a checksum manifest for runtime components used by your inference runtime (we do not need full source tarballs; checksums + provenance are fine).
- CAIQ responses for network segmentation / data residency questions (any partial responses are acceptable if flagged).
- Pointer to your SOC 2 report or the SOC point of contact; if there's a vendor performing independent attestation, please provide their contact.

Timing: we are targeting our internal review by 9/10. Would you be able to provide a first-pass package + brief attestation by early next week? If helpful, Tom Rivers (copied) from Auditus will be coordinating the evidence intake for us.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Nora
Nora Patel
Head of Platform Security, Nimble Health
N: +1 415-555-0123

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Supply-chain and interoperability evidence request (SOC2/SIG/CAIQ)

Nora —

Thanks for the clear checklist. We can get you a scoped bundle that hits each bullet. Quick summary of what we'll provide by 9/2 EOD (PST):

1) Subprocessor Census (spreadsheet): full roster, function, data types processed, location, contract link and whether they have direct data access.
2) SBOM checksum manifest: top-layer runtime components + provenance URL; we will not include source artifacts in the bundle but will include checksums and build IDs.
3) CAIQ partial responses: network segmentation, perimeter controls, and key-management (we will flag any unanswered items).
4) SOC 2: pointer to our SOC 2 assessor and the control owner for any follow-ups (we cannot attach the full report in public mail but can share through an NDA link).

I'm attaching the initial subprocessor census and the CAIQ draft. Laura will own the SBOM checksums and Evelyn will coordinate the SOC2 attestation logistics (NDA / access).

Proposed next steps:
- We upload the evidence bundle to a secure Drive link and share it with your security mailbox.
- Tom (Auditus) can drop any specific intake requirements to expedite.

If that timeline works I'll proceed.

— Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 650-555-0190

Ben —

This is perfect, thank you. A few clarifying items from our side before you upload: 

- For the subprocessor roster, could you flag any components that are used in multi-tenant hosted mode vs. dedicated/private (we need to confirm isolation guarantees for our regulated workloads).
- On the SBOM manifest: please include the build IDs + sha256 checksums for the inference-serving binary and any native kernels. A small note about which runtime pieces are considered "redwood-managed" vs customer-deployed would be helpful.
- Regarding SOC2: if you can provide the assessor contact (or a read-only portal link) that would reduce back-and-forth.

Tom — can you confirm your preferred intake format? We can accept a shared Drive folder with a short index file (index.md) that maps attachments to controls.

Appreciate the coordinated handoff.

— Nora
